title: facade catalogue - two masses
subtitle: Every scheme the grammar can say, on more than one building. Each card is a drawing set, not a picture: the elevations are dimensioned to the millimetre and every metric below is recomputed from the grammar when this page is built.

candidates.note: A bent-bar terrace bridge: the bar touches the ground at one entrance pier only, everything else cantilevers from z=1.861. 37 facets, widths 0.02 to 5.5 m.
A plain extruded prism: 35 vertices, two z levels, every vertical face a full rectangle, five storeys, sixteen facets. It sits on the ground and it does not step.

sections.title: Authored under the per-terminal depth table
sections.note: Two blind authors, one mass each, both accepted on attempt one with zero faults. The prism author read the new brief, which states a maximum depth per terminal; the bent-bar author read a stale one that still said 0.5 m for everything. The difference is the crown.

cards.title: Crown
cards.intent: A giant order of 13.22 m pilasters under a three-part termination - string course, arched arcade, five modillions, and a cornice projecting 0.70 m. The author wrote 0.70 because the brief said a cornice may reach 1.2; the bracket course exists to justify the overhang.

cards.title: Level eaves
cards.intent: Every horizontal hung off the storey axis rather than off the facet it lands on, so the cornice holds one line at 9.90 across a mass whose facets start at seven different heights. Its cornice is 0.30 m - the old flat ceiling - because this author was handed the stale brief.

sections.title: Schemes
sections.note: Every one authored by a repo-blind subagent from the brief alone, then held to the same gates the paid director applies.

cards.title: A beam that lands once
cards.intent: An author given no design intent read the mass itself - four of thirty-seven facets touch the ground, three of them one stem - and drew a lifted gallery. Level at the top, level at the underside, mass between: the two datums doing the same job at both ends
cards.axes: stone · accepted attempt 1 · bottom line 1.8609 m, six facets rise to it · every tier head now lands on 6.25 m whatever its own step

cards.title: Ends on one line
cards.intent: The mass steps; the building does not. Full-height piers carry a crown that rises to the building's top line, so the elevation ends level instead of on the steps
cards.axes: stone · accepted attempt 1 · the author found the rise datum in the brief unaided and guarded which facets may use it

cards.title: Live director
cards.intent: gpt-5.5 authoring unaided — the first facade a paid run has drawn on a mass that is not a prism
cards.axes: scores 100/100/97/100/88/100 · $0.12 · ninth attempt after eight failures

cards.title: Held by a datum
cards.intent: One continuous line at each floor, running the whole building on every elevation — the first scheme here whose horizontals cross the mass's own steps
cards.axes: limestone / deep / bronze / morning · accepted attempt 1 · 50 bands + 45 cornices at 3.30 / 6.60 / 9.30

cards.title: Unitised curtain wall
cards.intent: A continuous glazed skin hung in front of the structure — 100 mm mullions running past every floor, a spandrel at each slab, glass turning the corners
cards.axes: precast / clear / iron / morning · accepted on attempt 1 · all four layers, free lane

cards.title: Brise-soleil
cards.intent: Tropical modernism — deep horizontal blades standing over the glass on three faces, the fourth left plain
cards.axes: precast / deep / bronze / golden · accepted on attempt 1 · 42 louvres · four levels of scale

sections.title: The same grammar on a prism
sections.note: A mass that does not step. Nothing here is a new idea - these are schemes the same engine drew on a plain extruded block, and they are on this page because a catalogue of one building cannot tell you whether a facade is stepped by choice or by inheritance.

cards.title: Light frame
cards.intent: The best facade this project produced on the prism: a 0.3 m fold pier in bright precast with only a 40 mm mullion at the glass edge

cards.title: Glazed skin
cards.intent: Glass running five storeys, mullions unbroken grade to cornice, a spandrel at every slab

cards.title: Prism G
cards.intent: The scheme that reads best by eye of the eight first-round blind designs

cards.title: Prism H
cards.intent: Mixed construction on a prism - skin backs against a punched front

cards.title: Prism C
cards.intent: A deeply glazed frame; punched openings that happen to be large

cards.title: Transparent base
cards.intent: Weight inverted: a glazed ground storey under a closed body

sections.title: Material axes
sections.note: The same geometry under different wall, glass, frame and light. Nothing about the grammar changes between these - the scheme is one derivation and these are four readings of it, which is the point of keeping presentation outside the gated chain.
